statement: Let X, Y be smooth integral projective complex varieties, let W be normal and projective, and let X p ← − − W f − − → Y be morphisms, with p birational and f surjective and equidimensional. Identify C(Y ) with its induced subfield of C(X) = C(W). Fix a centered discrete valuation v of C(X), allowing also the zero valuation. Let A ≥ 0 be a rational divisor on Y such that p∗f∗A = 0. Let D0, D1 be rational Cartier divisors on X and put D(t) = (1 − t)D0 + tD1 (0 ≤ t ≤ 1). For each prime divisor Q of Y , define P(t) = ∑ Q min E: f(E)=Q coeffE p∗D(t) ordE(f∗Q) Q, (2.3) where E ranges over the prime divisors of W dominating Q. Assume that P(t) = (1−t)P(0)+tP(1) throughout [0, 1]. Suppose that rational numbers tj ∈ [0, 1] tend to zero and that hj ∈ C(Y )× ⊗Z Q satisfy Nj = D(tj) + divX(hj) ≥ 0, v(Nj) −→ 0. Finally, suppose that for some ϵ ∈ Q>0 and integer k > 0, the divisors B1 = k ( A + ϵP(1) ) , B0 = k ( A + ϵP(0) ) are Cartier and the ring R(Y ; B1, B0) is finitely generated. Then there is an effective rational divisor N ∼Q D0, v(N) = 0.
